title: Preservation timeline
subject: Islamic Studies
source: Seeded from islamic-studies/y7 lesson 13 (Pupil PDF worksheet: preservation timeline)
intro: Lesson 13: How hadith were preserved: memory, writing and the great collections. To understand how the hadith were preserved from the time of the Companions to the great collections

timeline.label: Lifetime
timeline.text: Companions hear, memorise and some write

timeline.label: c. 100 AH
timeline.text: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz orders gathering

questions.q: Put in order: Sahih al-Bukhari; Companions memorise; Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz's order; the Followers learn.
questions.a: Companions memorise; the Followers learn; Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz's order; Sahih al-Bukhari
questions.model: I do: the Companions heard him first, so they come first. The Followers (Tabi'un) learnt from them. Around 100 AH the caliph ordered gathering. Al-Bukhari wrote his Sahih in the 3rd century.

questions.q: Which Companion narrated the most hadith?
Name the two most authentic hadith books.
Make a five-stage timeline of how hadith were preserved, with one sentence per stage, in the pupil PDF or portal response box.
questions.a: Companions (memory, some writing); Followers; Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz's order; early books such as the Muwatta'; the great collections of al-Bukhari and Muslim.
questions.model: Teacher completes stage 1: 'The Companions heard the Prophet ﷺ, memorised his words and some, such as Abdullah ibn Amr, wrote them down.'

questions.q: explain why travelling to check one hadith shows how careful the early Muslims were.
questions.a: They wanted to hear it directly from the narrator to be sure of every word, not rely on rumours.

questions.q: why do you think a chain of names makes a report more trustworthy?
questions.a: Each person can be checked for honesty and memory, so a fake or mistaken link can be found.

questions.q: Sahih al-Bukhari was written in which century AH?
Back to our ponder: how did words from 1,400 years ago reach us accurately?
questions.a: Memory, writing, checking narrators, chains and great collections.
